Public type alias for the internal llhttp parser struct. Instances represent a parser state machine for HTTP/RTSP messages. Construct via llhttp_init on caller-allocated storage or llhttp_alloc for heap allocation; release with llhttp_free if allocated. Must be initialized before use.
Configuration struct holding user callback function pointers invoked during parsing. Must outlive the parser; initialize with llhttp_settings_init before assigning handlers.

objects.definition: typedef int (*llhttp_data_cb)(llhttp_t*, const char *at, size_t length);
objects.description: Function pointer type for callbacks that receive a data slice (pointer and length) during parsing. Return 0 on success, negative or specific HPE_* to signal errors or pauses.
Function pointer type for simple event callbacks that receive only the parser pointer. Return 0 on success, or error/pause codes as documented.

functions.name: llhttp__internal_init
functions.description: Initializes an llhttp internal parser state structure. Intended for internal use by the library (not the public API).
requirements: s must be a valid, writable pointer to an llhttp__internal_t instance
Caller should treat this as an internal API and prefer public llhttp_init/llhttp_alloc for normal usage

functions.name: llhttp__internal_execute
functions.signature: int llhttp__internal_execute(llhttp__internal_t* s, const char* p, const char* endp);
functions.description: Executes the internal llhttp state machine over a buffer range [p, endp). Intended for internal use by the library.
requirements: s must be an initialized llhttp__internal_t parser
p must be a valid pointer to the start of the input buffer; endp must be either p or a later pointer within the same buffer region
The range [p, endp) must be accessible for reading

functions.name: llhttp_init
functions.signature: void llhttp_init(llhttp_t* parser, llhttp_type_t type, const llhttp_settings_t* settings);
functions.description: Initializes a parser with the specified HTTP parsing type and user-provided callback settings. Use this when managing the parser memory yourself.
requirements: parser must be a valid, writable pointer
type must be one of llhttp_type_t (HTTP_BOTH, HTTP_REQUEST, HTTP_RESPONSE)
settings must point to a valid llhttp_settings_t whose lifetime is at least as long as parser (static or heap allocated)

functions.name: llhttp_alloc
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new parser instance of the given type; counterpart to llhttp_free.
requirements: type must be a valid llhttp_type_t value
Returned pointer must be freed with llhttp_free when no longer needed

functions.name: llhttp_free
functions.description: Frees a parser previously created by llhttp_alloc.
requirements: parser must be a pointer obtained from llhttp_alloc (or NULL if implementation allows; behavior for NULL is not specified)
Do not use parser after this call

functions.name: llhttp_get_type
functions.description: Returns the parser type (request/response/both) as an 8-bit value corresponding to llhttp_type_t.
requirements: parser must be a valid parser (initialized or allocated)

functions.name: llhttp_get_http_major
functions.description: Returns the parsed HTTP major version for the current message.
requirements: parser must be a valid parser (initialized or allocated)
Meaningful only after the start line has been parsed

functions.name: llhttp_get_http_minor
functions.description: Returns the parsed HTTP minor version for the current message.
requirements: parser must be a valid parser (initialized or allocated)
Meaningful only after the start line has been parsed

functions.name: llhttp_get_method
functions.description: Returns the parsed HTTP method as an 8-bit code (llhttp_method_t) for request messages.
requirements: parser must be a valid parser (initialized or allocated)
Only meaningful for request parsing (HTTP_REQUEST/HTTP_BOTH when a request is being parsed)

functions.name: llhttp_get_status_code
functions.description: Returns the parsed HTTP status code for response messages.
requirements: parser must be a valid parser (initialized or allocated)
Only meaningful for response parsing (HTTP_RESPONSE/HTTP_BOTH when a response is being parsed)

functions.name: llhttp_get_upgrade
functions.description: Returns whether the current message indicates an upgrade (non-zero if upgrade).
requirements: parser must be a valid parser (initialized or allocated)
Value is meaningful after headers are parsed

functions.name: llhttp_reset
functions.description: Resets an already initialized parser to the start state while preserving parser type, callback settings, user data, and lenient flags.
requirements: parser must be previously initialized via llhttp_init or created via llhttp_alloc

functions.name: llhttp_settings_init
functions.description: Initializes a settings object, typically zeroing callbacks and establishing defaults before assigning user callbacks.
requirements: settings must be a valid, writable pointer to llhttp_settings_t

functions.name: llhttp_execute
functions.signature: llhttp_errno_t llhttp_execute(llhttp_t* parser, const char* data, size_t len);
functions.description: Parses a buffer containing full or partial HTTP data, invoking callbacks as parsing proceeds. Returns an llhttp_errno_t indicating success, pause, or error.
requirements: parser must be initialized or allocated and configured with callbacks (settings)
data must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes
If any llhttp_data_cb returns an errno != HPE_OK, parsing stops and that errno is returned
If HPE_PAUSED is returned, resume later with llhttp_resume
On CONNECT/Upgrade, HPE_PAUSED_UPGRADE may be returned after fully parsing the message; continue with llhttp_resume_after_upgrade if desired
If a non-pause error is returned, subsequent calls will keep returning the same error until llhttp_init is called again

functions.name: llhttp_finish
functions.description: Signals that the input stream has ended (peer will send no more bytes). Completes messages that require EOF and may invoke on_message_complete. Returns an llhttp_errno_t.
requirements: Call when the other side has no further bytes to send (EOF/shutdown of readable side)
parser must be valid/initialized
If the request is safely terminated, on_message_complete will be invoked; otherwise an error code is returned

functions.name: llhttp_message_needs_eof
functions.description: Returns 1 if the current message requires EOF to be considered complete (llhttp_finish must be called to complete it).
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer to a parser (const OK)

functions.name: llhttp_should_keep_alive
functions.description: Returns 1 if additional messages may follow the last successfully parsed message (connection should be kept alive).
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer to a parser (const OK)

functions.name: llhttp_pause
functions.description: Forces subsequent llhttp_execute calls to return HPE_PAUSED and sets an appropriate error reason. Do not call from user callbacks.
requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
Must not be called from within user callbacks; callbacks should instead return HPE_PAUSED to request a pause

functions.name: llhttp_resume
functions.description: Resumes parsing after a pause requested by user callbacks (HPE_PAUSED).
requirements: Call only after llhttp_execute returned HPE_PAUSED
parser must be valid/initialized

functions.name: llhttp_resume_after_upgrade
functions.description: Resumes parsing after a full CONNECT/Upgrade message when llhttp_execute returned HPE_PAUSED_UPGRADE.
requirements: Call only after llhttp_execute returned HPE_PAUSED_UPGRADE
parser must be valid/initialized

functions.name: llhttp_get_errno
functions.description: Returns the most recent error code produced by the parser.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer (const OK)

functions.name: llhttp_get_error_reason
functions.description: Returns the textual reason associated with the last error. User callbacks can set this via llhttp_set_error_reason.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer (const OK)
Meaningful after an error or when a callback sets an error reason

functions.name: llhttp_set_error_reason
functions.signature: void llhttp_set_error_reason(llhttp_t* parser, const char* reason);
functions.description: Assigns a descriptive string to be associated with an error. Should be called by user callbacks immediately before returning an error code (e.g., HPE_USER).
requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
reason must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string that remains valid for as long as needed to read it later (lifetime not specified; typical practice is static or externally owned storage)
Should be called from within user callbacks right before returning the errno

functions.name: llhttp_get_error_pos
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the last parsed byte before the error. The pointer is relative to the data buffer passed to llhttp_execute.
requirements: parser must be a valid pointer (const OK)
Only meaningful after llhttp_execute has returned an error

functions.name: llhttp_errno_name
functions.description: Returns the textual name of an llhttp error code.
requirements: err must be a valid llhttp_errno_t value

functions.name: llhttp_method_name
functions.description: Returns the textual name of an HTTP method code.
requirements: method must be a valid llhttp_method_t value

functions.name: llhttp_status_name
functions.description: Returns the textual name of an HTTP status code.
requirements: status must be a valid llhttp_status_t value

functions.name: llhttp_set_lenient_headers
functions.description: Enables or disables lenient parsing of header values (disables header value token checks). Security-sensitive; use with caution.
requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
enabled is treated as boolean: non-zero enables, zero disables
Enabling increases exposure to request smuggling; caller must assess security impact

functions.name: llhttp_set_lenient_chunked_length
functions.description: Enables or disables lenient handling of conflicting Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length headers. Security-sensitive.
requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
enabled is treated as boolean: non-zero enables, zero disables
Enabling increases exposure to request smuggling; caller must assess security impact

functions.name: llhttp_set_lenient_keep_alive
functions.description: Enables or disables lenient handling of Connection: close and HTTP/1.0 request/response sequencing. Security-sensitive.
requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
enabled is treated as boolean: non-zero enables, zero disables
Enabling increases exposure to poisoning attacks; caller must assess security impact

functions.name: llhttp_set_lenient_transfer_encoding
functions.description: Enables or disables lenient handling of Transfer-Encoding values after 'chunked'. Security-sensitive.
requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
enabled is treated as boolean: non-zero enables, zero disables
Enabling increases exposure to request smuggling; caller must assess security impact

functions.description: Enables or disables lenient handling of non-standard HTTP versions. Security-sensitive.
requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
enabled is treated as boolean: non-zero enables, zero disables
Enabling allows unsupported HTTP versions; caller must assess security impact

functions.description: Enables or disables lenient handling of extra data received after a message ends when keep-alive is disabled. Security-sensitive.
requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
enabled is treated as boolean: non-zero enables, zero disables
Enabling increases exposure to poisoning attacks; caller must assess security impact

enabled is treated as boolean: non-zero enables, zero disables
Enabling increases exposure to request smuggling; caller must assess security impact

functions.description: Enables or disables lenient handling where LF does not need to be preceded by CR to terminate sections. Security-sensitive.
requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
enabled is treated as boolean: non-zero enables, zero disables
Enabling increases exposure to request smuggling; caller must assess security impact

requirements: parser must be valid/initialized
enabled is treated as boolean: non-zero enables, zero disables

data_types.description: Arbitrary byte sequence representing HTTP/1.x or RTSP protocol data. This may include request/response start lines, headers separated by CRLF, optional bodies (including chunked transfer encoding), and may be partial fragments of a message. Data can contain any bytes, not necessarily NUL-terminated, and may include upgrades or CONNECT semantics.

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid HTTP/1.x or RTSP messages and fragments.
# It aims to cover:
# - Requests (various methods, paths, versions)
# - Responses (various status codes/reasons, versions)
# - Headers with diverse semantics (Connection, Transfer-Encoding, Content-Length, Upgrade, Host, etc.)
# - Bodies: fixed length, chunked (with optional extensions), empty, and upgrade prefaces
# - Partial buffers: prefixes, suffixes, and interior slices of messages to exercise streaming parsers
# - RTSP variants (different methods and versions)
#
# The fuzz stubs select arbitrary subranges of the provided string, so we try to build
# messages that remain valid over many sub-slices.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096

_HTTP_METHODS = [
    # Core HTTP
    "GET", "POST", "HEAD", "PUT", "DELETE", "OPTIONS", "TRACE", "PATCH", "CONNECT",
    # WebDAV/others
    "COPY", "LOCK", "MKCOL", "MOVE", "PROPFIND", "PROPPATCH", "UNLOCK", "BIND", "REBIND", "UNBIND",
    "ACL", "REPORT", "MKACTIVITY", "CHECKOUT", "MERGE", "LINK", "UNLINK", "PURGE",
    # RTSP/extra per llhttp
    "MSEARCH", "NOTIFY", "SUBSCRIBE", "UNSUBSCRIBE", "MKCALENDAR", "SOURCE", "PRI",
    # RTSP methods
    "DESCRIBE", "ANNOUNCE", "SETUP", "PLAY", "PAUSE", "TEARDOWN", "GET_PARAMETER",
    "SET_PARAMETER", "REDIRECT", "RECORD", "FLUSH", "QUERY",
]

_HTTP_VERSIONS = ["HTTP/1.0", "HTTP/1.1"]
_RTSP_VERSIONS = ["RTSP/1.0"]

_STATUS_LINES = [
    (200, "OK"), (201, "Created"), (202, "Accepted"), (204, "No Content"),
    (206, "Partial Content"), (301, "Moved Permanently"), (302, "Found"), (303, "See Other"),
    (307, "Temporary Redirect"), (308, "Permanent Redirect"),
    (400, "Bad Request"), (401, "Unauthorized"), (403, "Forbidden"), (404, "Not Found"),
    (405, "Method Not Allowed"), (408, "Request Timeout"), (411, "Length Required"),
    (413, "Payload Too Large"), (414, "URI Too Long"), (415, "Unsupported Media Type"),
    (418, "I'm a teapot"), (426, "Upgrade Required"), (429, "Too Many Requests"),
    (431, "Request Header Fields Too Large"),
    (500, "Internal Server Error"), (501, "Not Implemented"), (502, "Bad Gateway"),
    (503, "Service Unavailable"), (504, "Gateway Timeout"), (505, "HTTP Version Not Supported"),
]

_HEADER_NAMES = [
    "Host", "User-Agent", "Accept", "Accept-Encoding", "Accept-Language", "Connection",
    "Content-Type", "Content-Length", "Transfer-Encoding", "Upgrade", "TE",
    "Trailer", "Pragma", "Cache-Control", "Expect", "Via", "Referer", "Range",
    "Authorization", "Proxy-Authorization", "X-Test", "Custom-Header",
]

_UPGRADES = ["websocket", "h2c", "SPDY/3.1"]

    "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "application/json", "application/octet-stream", "text/html",

# Helpers

def _rand_rfc_token(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    tchars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~"
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(tchars) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_lws(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Linear whitespace variants
    choices = [" ", "\t", "  ", "\t ", " \t", " \t "]
    return r.choice(choices)

def _rand_host(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        # IPv6 literal
        hexd = ''.join(r.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(r.randint(2, 4)))
        return f"[{hexd}:{hexd}::{hexd}]"
    parts = [
        ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 8)))
        for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3))
    ]
    host = '.'.join(parts)
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        host += f":{r.randint(1, 65535)}"
    return host

def _rand_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    segs = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 5)):
        seg = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~") for _ in range(r.randint(1, 10)))
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            seg += '%{:02X}'.format(r.randint(0, 255))
        segs.append(seg)
    path = '/' + '/'.join(segs)
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        # query
        qn = r.randint(1, 4)
        pairs = []
        for _ in range(qn):
            k = _rand_rfc_token(r, 1, 8)
            v = _rand_rfc_token(r, 0, 8)
            pairs.append(f"{k}={v}")
        path += '?' + '&'.join(pairs)
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        # fragment
        path += '#' + _rand_rfc_token(r, 1, 6)
    return path

def _headers_base(r: random.Random, is_request: bool, body_len: int, chunked: bool, upgrade: bool, close_conn: bool, is_rtsp: bool) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    headers: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    if is_request:
        headers.append(("Host", _rand_host(r)))
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        headers.append(("User-Agent", r.choice(_UA)))
    if upgrade:
        headers.append(("Upgrade", r.choice(_UPGRADES)))
        headers.append(("Connection", "Upgrade"))
    else:
        if close_conn:
            headers.append(("Connection", "close"))
        elif r.random() < 0.5:
            headers.append(("Connection", "keep-alive"))
    if chunked:
        headers.append(("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked"))
        # Optional TE header (requests) per HTTP/1.1
        if is_request and r.random() < 0.3:
            headers.append(("TE", "trailers"))
    else:
        headers.append(("Content-Length", str(body_len)))
    if r.random() < 0.5 and body_len > 0:
        headers.append(("Content-Type", r.choice(_CONTENT_TYPES)))
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        headers.append(("Accept-Encoding", "gzip, deflate"))
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        headers.append(("Accept-Language", "en-US,en;q=0.9"))
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        headers.append(("Pragma", "no-cache"))
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        headers.append(("Cache-Control", "no-cache"))
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        headers.append(("X-Test", _rand_rfc_token(r, 3, 12)))
    # For chunked, sometimes add Trailer header to exercise trailing headers support
    if chunked and r.random() < 0.5:
        headers.append(("Trailer", "X-Trailer, Expires"))
    # RTSP specific headers are similar but we keep generic for valid parsing
    return headers

def _render_headers(r: random.Random, headers: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
    # Randomize header order slightly
    r.shuffle(headers)
    lines = []
    for k, v in headers:
        if r.random() < 0.15:
            # Add optional obs-fold-like whitespace around colon
            lines.append(f"{k}{_rand_lws(r)}:{_rand_lws(r)}{v}\r\n")
        else:
            lines.append(f"{k}: {v}\r\n")
    return ''.join(lines) + "\r\n"

def _make_chunked_body(r: random.Random) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    # Build chunked body with 1-5 chunks, optional extensions, and optional small trailers
    nchunks = r.randint(1, 5)
    chunks = []
    plain = []
    for _ in range(nchunks):
        size = r.randint(0, 64)
        data = ''.join(r.choice(string.printable[:95]) for _ in range(size))
        plain.append(data)
        ext = ''
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            ext_name = _rand_rfc_token(r, 1, 6)
            ext_val = _rand_rfc_token(r, 0, 6)
            if ext_val:
                ext = f";{ext_name}={ext_val}"
            else:
                ext = f";{ext_name}"
        chunks.append(f"{size:x}{ext}\r\n{data}\r\n")
    # last-chunk
    body = ''.join(chunks) + "0\r\n"
    # Optional trailer headers
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        body += f"X-Trailer: {_rand_rfc_token(r,4,10)}\r\n"
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            body += f"Expires: {r.randint(0, 999999)}\r\n"
    body += "\r\n"
    return body, ''.join(plain)

def _make_fixed_body(r: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Simple ASCII payload with some variability
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_.:/[]{}()\n\r\t"
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _build_request(r: random.Random) -> str:
    is_rtsp = r.random() < 0.25
    method = r.choice(_HTTP_METHODS)
    if is_rtsp and method not in [
        "DESCRIBE","ANNOUNCE","SETUP","PLAY","PAUSE","TEARDOWN","GET_PARAMETER",
        "SET_PARAMETER","REDIRECT","RECORD","FLUSH","QUERY"]:
        # For RTSP prefer RTSP methods
        method = r.choice(["DESCRIBE","ANNOUNCE","SETUP","PLAY","PAUSE","TEARDOWN","GET_PARAMETER",
                           "SET_PARAMETER","REDIRECT","RECORD","FLUSH","QUERY"])
    version = r.choice(_RTSP_VERSIONS if is_rtsp else _HTTP_VERSIONS)

    # Request-URI: absolute form for proxies sometimes
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        scheme = "rtsp" if is_rtsp else "http"
        uri = f"{scheme}://{_rand_host(r)}{_rand_path(r)}"
    else:
        uri = _rand_path(r)

    # Decide body/encoding
    upgrade = (method == "CONNECT") or (not is_rtsp and method in ("PRI",) and r.random() < 0.5)
    has_body_methods = method in ("POST", "PUT", "PATCH") or (is_rtsp and method in ("ANNOUNCE", "SET_PARAMETER", "RECORD"))
    chunked = (not is_rtsp) and has_body_methods and r.random() < 0.5
    body_len = r.randint(0, 256) if has_body_methods and not chunked else 0
    close_conn = r.random() < 0.2

    start = f"{method} {uri} {version}\r\n"
    headers = _headers_base(r, True, body_len, chunked, upgrade, close_conn, is_rtsp)

    msg = start + _render_headers(r, headers)

    if chunked:
        body, _ = _make_chunked_body(r)
        msg += body
    elif body_len > 0:
        body = _make_fixed_body(r, body_len)
        msg += body
    # CONNECT usually has no body
    return msg

def _build_response(r: random.Random) -> str:
    version = r.choice(_HTTP_VERSIONS)
    code, reason = r.choice(_STATUS_LINES)
    start = f"{version} {code} {reason}\r\n"

    # Responses with body typically for codes not in [1xx, 204, 304]
    body_permitted = not (100 <= code < 200 or code in (204, 304))

    # Decide upgrade/chunked/length
    upgrade = (code == 101 and r.random() < 0.7) or (code == 426 and r.random() < 0.4)
    chunked = body_permitted and r.random() < 0.5
    body_len = r.randint(0, 256) if body_permitted and not chunked else 0
    close_conn = r.random() < 0.2

    headers = _headers_base(r, False, body_len, chunked, upgrade, close_conn, False)
    # Some response-specific headers
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        headers.append(("Server", _rand_rfc_token(r, 3, 10)))
    if r.random() < 0.2 and body_permitted:
        headers.append(("ETag", '"' + _rand_rfc_token(r, 6, 12) + '"'))
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        headers.append(("Date", "Sat, 07 Jan 2023 12:34:56 GMT"))

    msg = start + _render_headers(r, headers)
    if chunked:
        body, _ = _make_chunked_body(r)
        msg += body
    elif body_len > 0:
        body = _make_fixed_body(r, body_len)
        msg += body
    return msg

def _maybe_concat_messages(r: random.Random, first: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes chain multiple messages to exercise keep-alive pipelines
    out = [first]
    count = 1 + (0 if r.random() < 0.6 else r.randint(1, 2))  # up to 3 messages
    for _ in range(1, count):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            out.append(_build_request(r))
        else:
            out.append(_build_response(r))
    return ''.join(out)

def _maybe_partial_slice(r: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Produce a valid subsequence to simulate streaming fragments
    if len(data) == 0 or r.random() < 0.3:
        return data
    n = len(data)
    i0 = r.randint(0, n)
    i1 = r.randint(0, n)
    if i0 > i1:
        i0, i1 = i1, i0
    return data[i0:i1]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose to build a request or response first
    if r.random() < 0.55:
        msg = _build_request(r)
    else:
        msg = _build_response(r)

    # Sometimes concatenate additional messages to simulate keep-alive
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        msg = _maybe_concat_messages(r, msg)

    # Ensure size cap
    if len(msg) > _MAX_SIZE:
        msg = msg[:_MAX_SIZE]

    data = msg.encode('ascii', errors='strict')

    # The harness for llhttp__internal_execute already picks a subrange; for variety we sometimes
    # pre-slice to create smaller valid fragments. This remains valid since stubs may further slice.
    data = _maybe_partial_slice(r, data)

    # Final size guard
    if len(data) > _MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:_MAX_SIZE]

    return data
